rationale: Likely Lycopolitan qualitative form of ⲛⲁϣⲉ/ⲛⲟϭ 'be great.' Parallel structure ⲛⲁϯ X ⲛⲁϯ Y suggests acclamatory 'great is X, great is Y.' Awaits confirmation in further contexts.
Agent-noun on root ⲱⲣϫ/ⲱⲣϩ 'guard, watch.' Distinct from accumulated ⲁϩⲟⲩⲱⲣⲟⲩⲱⲣⲉϩ 'keep guard' as a substantival form.
Hydrological-cosmological term meaning 'spring, well.' Used metaphorically of the 'living spring' that gushes forth (ⲃⲉⲃⲉ) in those who thirst.
Plural participle/relative on Lycopolitan ⲁⲃⲉ for ⲉⲓⲃⲉ 'thirst.' Confirmed by collocation 'gushing forth ... that they may drink (ⲥⲱ) and live.'

Plural of ϩⲃⲱⲥ 'covering, garment.' In Manichaean cosmology, the layered 'coverings' of the cosmos = the firmaments (paralleled in line 24 by Greek loanword ϩⲁⲡⲗⲱⲙⲁ = ἁπλώματα 'spread-out things, firmaments').
ϩⲁⲗⲡⲉ = ϩⲉⲗⲡⲉ 'navel.' Cosmic-anatomical correspondent of the sphere of stars.
Lycopolitan plural on ⲥⲡⲓⲣ 'rib.' Body-part in the cosmic-anatomical correspondence series.
Possibly Lycopolitan reflex of ⲕⲉϩⲥ 'loin' or related body-part term. Position in the descending cosmic-anatomical series (after navel, before feet) supports lower-body reading.
Plural body-part term paired with 'their feet.' Etymology uncertain; possibly Lycopolitan plural 'shins/calves/legs.'
Body-part term following 'neck' in the descending cosmic-anatomical sequence. Etymology unclear; awaits parallel attestations.
Possibly Lycopolitan form of ⲅⲉⲛⲉⲁ 'generation' or related to ⲗⲁⲏ/λαός 'people' (in accumulated vocabulary). 'Of your generation' fits apostolic-instructional context.
Idiom — ⲡⲓⲟⲩⲉ + ⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'one' likely means 'in one and the same (manner/place).' Functions adverbially.
Lycopolitan ⲡⲁⲭⲉ + suffix ⲩ (= ⲛⲁϥ?) functioning as 'he said to him.' The -ⲩ ending appears as a dative-bound form rather than the standard 3pl ⲡⲉϫⲁⲩ 'they said.'
